standard.title: Apply spoken conventions for fluency in familiar and unfamiliar contexts
standard.description: apply features and conventions of spoken target language to extend fluency in responding to and creating texts in familiar and unfamiliar contexts
standard.prior_knowledge: Students apply spoken target language conventions including consonant nuances, sentence-level stress, written doubling conventions and extended intonation (AC9LS8U01). They apply these in familiar contexts. They have not yet applied spoken conventions in genuinely unfamiliar contexts, nor created extended spoken texts for real audiences.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students apply spoken conventions to extend fluency — including natural speech features, extended sentence stress, and authentic spoken production — in familiar and unfamiliar contexts.

nodes.label: Natural speech features and extended sentence stress
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can apply natural speech features — contractions, elision, rhythm — and place stress correctly in extended and complex sentences.
nodes.minimum_width: Demonstrate at least two natural speech features in connected speech; place stress correctly across at least two complex sentences.
nodes.typical_width: Apply contractions, elision and natural rhythm in connected speech; maintain stress patterns in complex sentences; develop fluency through tongue twisters, reading aloud and performance; apply spoken conventions in unrehearsed contexts.
wider: Produce a recording of connected speech demonstrating natural rhythm, elision and stress — compare with a native speaker sample and identify remaining differences
Apply spoken conventions in a genuine unrehearsed context — demonstrating that prosodic features are automatic rather than deliberate
nodes.hinge_reason: Natural speech features — contractions, elision, natural rhythm — are what distinguish fluent from stilted spoken production. Students who speak only in citation forms sound unnatural and are difficult to understand in authentic interaction.

response_modes.reason: Natural speech features become automatic only through high-frequency production in varied spoken contexts — including unrehearsed conditions. Rehearsed accuracy does not transfer automatically to natural speech.

success_criteria: Demonstrates at least two natural speech features in connected speech
Places stress correctly across at least two complex sentences

nodes.label: Fluency in unfamiliar contexts and spoken text creation
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can respond and create with adequate fluency in unfamiliar spoken contexts — applying all prior spoken conventions in extended unrehearsed production.
nodes.minimum_width: Produce an extended spoken text in an unfamiliar context with fluency adequate for the communicative purpose.
nodes.typical_width: Apply spoken conventions in unfamiliar and spontaneous contexts; create extended spoken texts — presentations, debates, interviews, performances — applying prosodic features deliberately; sustain spoken interaction without excessive hesitation or code-switching.
wider: Participate in a fully spontaneous spoken exchange on an unfamiliar topic — sustaining fluency for at least five minutes
Create and perform an original spoken text with deliberate prosodic design — demonstrate that intonation, stress and rhythm serve the communicative and expressive purpose

response_modes.reason: Fluency in unfamiliar contexts requires encountering genuinely varied and unpredictable spoken conditions. Rehearsed performance does not build the spontaneous spoken fluency that authentic interaction demands.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Spontaneous spoken fluency in unfamiliar contexts is the highest-order oral capability in the sequence — the benchmark for genuine communicative competence in the target language.
success_criteria: Produces an extended spoken text in an unfamiliar context with fluency adequate for communicative purpose
Applies natural speech features in at least one unrehearsed spoken context

nodes.label: Performing and recording spoken texts for real audiences
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can create and perform or record spoken texts for real audiences — applying all spoken conventions with deliberate expressive intent.
nodes.minimum_width: Create and deliver at least one spoken text for a real audience applying prosodic features deliberately.
nodes.typical_width: Create and perform debates, speeches, dramatisations, podcasts, interviews and recordings for real audiences; apply all spoken conventions — intonation, stress, rhythm, natural features — with deliberate expressive purpose; evaluate own spoken performance against authentic native speaker models.
wider: Create and record an extended spoken production — compare with an authentic native speaker text and reflect on every remaining difference
Perform a spoken text for a target language community audience — receive feedback and reflect on communicative effectiveness

response_modes.reason: Spoken performance for real audiences integrates all spoken convention capabilities — natural features (N1), spontaneous fluency (N2) — and deploys them for a genuine communicative purpose.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Creating and performing spoken texts for real target language community audiences is where spoken competence becomes genuinely purposeful — students are performing, not only practising.
success_criteria: Creates and delivers a spoken text for a real audience using prosodic features deliberately
The spoken text achieves its communicative or expressive purpose for the audience
